questions.q: Per this lesson, which sandbox type is used for final staging/UAT with a complete copy of production data and metadata?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Full
Partial Copy
questions.explain: A Full sandbox is a complete copy of production data and metadata, refreshed roughly every 29 days, used for final staging and user acceptance testing.

questions.q: What is a specific limitation of change sets that this lesson gives as a reason to use source-driven deployment instead?
options: Change sets have no version history, no built-in code review step, and make it easy to forget a dependency
Change sets cannot move custom objects
Change sets require a paid add-on license
Change sets can only be used in Developer Edition orgs
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out missing version history, no code review step, and easily forgotten dependencies as change sets' real limits for a project like this one.

questions.q: What does `sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --test-level RunLocalTests` actually enforce during deployment?
options: It skips all Apex tests to speed up deployment
It runs every Apex test in the org as part of the deployment, enforcing the 75% coverage requirement at deploy time
It only deploys Lightning Web Components, not Apex
It permanently deletes all existing metadata before deploying
questions.explain: RunLocalTests runs local Apex tests as part of the deployment itself, which is what actually enforces the coverage requirement rather than relying on someone remembering to check beforehand.

questions.q: What does the `--dry-run` flag do in `sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests`?
options: It permanently deploys the change immediately
It deletes the force-app directory
It disables Apex tests entirely
It validates the deployment (including running tests) without actually deploying the components
questions.explain: A dry run validates the deployment, including test execution, without actually committing the deployed components -- useful for checking a deployment will succeed before doing it for real.

questions.q: What does this lesson's CI pipeline do on every pull request against the repository?
options: It creates a fresh scratch org, deploys the full codebase into it, and runs all local Apex tests, blocking the merge if any step fails
Nothing automatic; a human must manually run tests before merging
It directly deploys every pull request straight to the production org
It only checks code formatting, not functional correctness
questions.explain: The pipeline creates a scratch org, deploys the codebase, and runs local Apex tests on every pull request, acting as a gate that blocks merging a pull request if any of that fails.
